subject: Reserved capacity commit: sizing tilt, pricing exposure & discount exception request
messages:
From: Eli Nguyen <eli.nguyen@novalabs.ai>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.ai>
Cc: Procurement <procure@novalabs.ai>
Date: 2028-03-15T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Capacity ask + pricing structure for Q3 launch

Jasmine,

Thanks again for the demo last week — NovaLabs is excited about Redwood's latency profile for low-latency chat inference. We are preparing an internal sizing request for a Q3 pilot and want to understand how Reserved capacity pricing behaves if GPU costs shift during our committed term.

Top of mind for procurement:
- We expect baseline steady throughput of ~60 p50 concurrent streams (avg seq len 512) with burst peaks to 140 for two 2-hour windows daily.
- Requesting 8-node reserved pool for a 24-month term to match our roadmap.
- Target discount: 28% off list for the committed pool; procurement wants confirmation of floor/ceiling if public GPU pricing moves >15%

Can you provide a simple sensitivity table that shows 3 scenarios (base, +20% GPU cost, -20% GPU cost) and the delta to per-token/unit price and to Redwood margin? We need that to justify the internal approval for a longer tenor.

Attachments: we attached our planned usage profile (NovaLabs_reserved_plan_v1.xlsx).

Best,
Eli
Director, ML Ops
NovaLabs

From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.ai>
To: Eli Nguyen <eli.nguyen@novalabs.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-03-15T11:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Capacity ask + pricing structure for Q3 launch

Eli — thanks for the clear asks and the workbook. Karthik / Marcus, looping you in for sizing and commercial input.

Quick answers while we run a sensitivity:
- We can provision a ded pool mapped to 8 nodes (we assume Aurora 80GB equivalent instances per node) and a burst lane for the 2-hour windows; we’ll sketch the autoscale/Burst config.
- Redwood pricing teams typically tie long-tenor discounts to a floor mechanism (protects both sides). For a 24-month commit at 8 nodes we can consider a two-way clause:
  * If underlying GPU raw-hour cost increases > 12% vs base, we escalate to a commercial review and have a pre-agreed pass-through band up to +10% (with exec approval required beyond that).
  * If GPU raw-hour cost decreases > 12%, we offer a rebate credit applied quarterly up to 8% of committed spend.

Karthik — can you run a model for the three scenarios Eli requested and attach the sensitivity outputs? Marcus — I’ll need your note on whether we can approve a 28% discount floor without exec sign-off or whether this requires Finance/RevOps approval.

Thanks,
Jasmine
Enterprise AE, Redwood Inference
Attachment: redwood-dedicated-commit-terms-draft.docx

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Eli Nguyen <eli.nguyen@novalabs.ai>
Date: 2028-03-16T08:37:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Capacity ask + pricing structure for Q3 launch

Jasmine / team,

Attached is a quick sensitivity export (pricing_sensitivity_model_2028.csv) — summary below:

Scenario A — Base (GPU cost = $1.00/hr baseline):
- Committed 8-node pool, list price per node: $X, committed unit price after 24 mo, 28% discount => blended per-token latency unit $0.00045
- Redwood estimated margin: ~34%

Scenario B — +20% GPU input cost:
- If we keep discount fixed at 28%: per-token price increases ~+14% (to $0.00051), margin down to ~24%
- With pre-agreed pass-through band (+10% cap without exec): per-token +7% only, margin ~29%

Scenario C — -20% GPU input cost:
- With rebate mechanics: per-token drops ~-9% (to $0.00041), estimated rebate credit applied quarterly; margin improves to ~38%

Recommended commercial constructs to present to NovaLabs:
1) Offer the 28% nominal discount with a two-way GPU-cost band: +/-12% no-change; within +12% to +22% we apply a pre-agreed pass-through of up to +10% (no margin protection beyond); beyond +22% we escalate to commercial execs for shared relief.
2) For decreases beyond -12% we automatically credit back up to 8% of committed spend applied quarterly.

Notes: these numbers assume stable seq lengths and continuous utilization per their workbook. If NovaLabs has higher tail bursts we need to size extra burst nodes (billed at on-demand).

-Karthik
Sr. Pricing Analyst, Redwood Inference

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Eli Nguyen <eli.nguyen@novalabs.ai>
Date: 2028-03-17T16:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Capacity ask + pricing structure for Q3 launch

Jasmine — quick commercial take / exec guidance.

1) 28% discount on a 24-month 8-node commit is approvable but requires RevOps sign-off because it pushes into strategic-customer discount bands. I can pre-approve up to 24% at manager level; anything >24% needs RevOps director sign-off. Please send the final commitment form and projected ARR so I can expedite.

2) The two-way GPU-cost band Karthik proposed is reasonable operationally. For risk management we prefer: +10% pass-through cap without exec, and an automatic rebate on downside up to 8% as a goodwill mechanism. Anything that exposes us to >15% margin compression needs Exec escalation.

3) Action items for Jasmine:
- Confirm final node spec (Aurora80 equiv) and exact expected burst hours per week.
- Share projected ARR and legal-signed PO if procurement accepts the two-way band.

Eli — if you can return the signed order form with PO number by 2028-03-24 we will route RevOps approval and lock in the 28% discount and the band in the SOW.

Marcus Lin
Head of Commercial Operations, Redwood Inference

On Fri, Mar 17, 2028 at 09:15 AM Eli Nguyen <eli.nguyen@novalabs.ai> wrote:
> Thanks — will review and get back with PO/ask. Appreciate the clarity on the band.
>
> -Eli
